hostap_config: re-enforce HT requirements Pure N should require HT support. We don't want to continue handicapping ourselves for daisy/snow. (Or at least, we shouldn't keep whining about this condition.) It happens that all supported devices now work fine with require_ht, so let's turn it back on. Per hostapd, "require_ht" and "require_vht" mean including the HT or VHT BSS selector in the Supported rates (or Extended supported rates) IE, which means that the client station must support HT or VHT in order to associate. It does *not* mean that the AP won't also advertise legacy (non-(V)HT) rates, and so clients are still allowed to regress from HT to legacy rates. Given the above, it's not 100% clear how we should translate 11xx_PURE into hostapd properties. Particularly, 11AC_PURE could be interpreted to mean: * require VHT or * require HT and VHT I've selected the former for now, as it's the least churn, but we can update this choice later if desired. CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Fix broken ble re-advertisement feature BLE advertisment needs to be re-enabled in kernel when previous ble connection goes away. This feature is broken from the commit 5084500d59bb ("CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event") in 11/2017, this feature is broken in cros kernel 3.10, 3.14, 3.18 and 4.4. I have verified this feature using several linux kernels, including 4.19.25 in raspi 3 + ble dongle, and confirm ble advertisment needs to be re-enabled in __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance from kernel bluetooth when previous BLE connection goes away. Confirm with Luiz Augusto von Denz from bluetooth upstream, BLE advertisement needs to be re-enabled by kernel when previous BLE connection goes away, this feature has been there in bluetooth kernel upstream for several years. The code logic is roughly as below. When BLE connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag needs to be cleared via hci_dev_clear_flag(hdev, HCI_LE_ADV) in hci_le_conn_complete_evt, Linux bluetooth use this flag to check if advertisment is there. a. When there is no ble connection and ble advertisment is there, __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is peridically called, and if that is just rescheduling the same instance, it does not execute any HCI command, and return since HCI_LE_ADV has been set, and it use same adv instance. b. When ble connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt. Then __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance would be periodically called, and it would goes to __hci_req_enable_advertising and does not enable advertisement since connection is there. c. When ble disconnection happens, when __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is called again, it found HCI_LE_ADV has been cleared in b, and goes to call __hci_req_enable_advertising, and found ble connection is not there, and re-enable ble advertisement. Regarding the chromium:776423, it seems the previous fix is not right, it should be addressed by the below ways a.by the controller, fix Connection Failed to be Established issues. b.in kernel side, from hci_cs_le_read_remote_features() of hci_event.c, when the return status is not successful, setting LE advertising flag to true if it is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt() previously in a connection attempt. c.Add "LE Set Advertise Enable" command with 0x00 (disabled) before the next "LE Set Advertising Parameters" command when hitting the error on LE read remote used features command. Either way, it should not break the ble re-advertisment feature. Revert "CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event" This reverts commit 5084500d59bb4e09b01d5323323b2cf7e0758611. BUG=chromium:939172 TEST=Local BLE connection test Change-Id: I7535bb09ddc25ef92b8774c55c0aff07599a52fb Signed-off-by: Yunhan Wang <yunhanw@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1506029 Reviewed-by: Martin Turon <mturon@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com> (cherry picked from commit 9b775c0d3990097245f8cf1ad5a77e3922235db8) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1512273 Reviewed-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org>
